topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the aims of the lecture, outlining how genetic mutations drive the hallmarks of cancer and tumor progression.

topics.label: Deregulation of Proliferation and Growth Signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in surface receptors and intracellular pathways, including Wnt/beta-catenin and RTK cascades, confer growth signal autonomy.

topics.label: Differentiation Block in Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how blocks in cellular differentiation prevent cells from reaching functional terminal states in leukemias and colorectal carcinomas.

topics.label: Resistance to Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how cancer cells evade programmed cell death through alterations in p53 signaling and the balance of pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality and Senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address how cancer cells overcome the Hayflick limit and cellular senescence via telomere maintenance and TERT reactivation, concluding the overview of growth control mechanisms.

topics.label: Altered Cancer Metabolism
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine metabolic rewiring in cancer, including the Warburg effect, aerobic glycolysis, and the generation of oncometabolites that induce epigenetic changes.

topics.label: Inducing Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumors stimulate new blood vessel growth to overcome hypoxia and nutrient diffusion limits through a shift in angiogenic regulators.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Progression of Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the multi-step metastatic cascade, covering invasion, transport through the circulation, seed-and-soil compatibility, and the clonal genetics of secondary tumors.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Summary
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by summarising the integration of cancer hallmarks and inviting questions from students.
